messages.author: 2d129c36308439da
messages.subject: Occupancy dependence among species
parts:
Hello all,
We are building a dynamic occupancy model for data from a long-term bird survey. Multiple species are recorded during the survey but we are interested in only 1, Species A. In addition to static or dynamic abiotic covariates on detection and occupancy of Species A we would like to add the presence of Species B as a covariate on occupancy. Can anyone point us to a discussion or manuscript that might give some example model formulation on how to do this? We will need to model occupancy of Species B in parallel with Species A and then add that occupancy as 0/1 to the covariates on Species A occupancy but not exactly sure how to do that. Thanks for any insight.

messages.author: 58a62321f08f30f8
messages.subject: RE: Occupancy dependence among species
parts:
Hi Tony,

 

Do you have access to ‘the Kery books’? I think there is an example in the Bayesian Pop Analysis book where the occupancy of a bird is modeled using estimated jointly with the occupancy of red squirrels – and then one (sqwurl), is used as a covariate on the other (bird). This is done using a Bayesian analysis due to the convenience of being able to estimate the latent z’s in the mcmc and use them in the linear predictor. So, for your uni-directional example (A influenced by B, but B not influenced by A), and where you aren’t necessarily interested in inferring co-occurrence, then I think this approach does what you need.

 

Let me know if you don’t have the book and I can fax you the relevant pages. It might also be the case that this is an example in one of the workshops I have attended, so, if it’s not in the book let me know and I will dig out that material too.

 

Good luck!

 

Chris

In addition to static or dynamic abiotic covariates on detection and occupancy of Species A we would like to add the presence of Species B as a covariate on occupancy. Can anyone point us to a discussion or manuscript that might give some example model formulation on how to do this? We will need to model occupancy of Species B in parallel with Species A and then add that occupancy as 0/1 to the covariates on Species A occupancy but not exactly sure how to do that. Thanks for any insight.

messages.subject: AW: Occupancy dependence among species
parts:
Dear Tony,

 

You need the model by Waddle et al. (EcolApp 2010) or Richmond et al. (same place and year). This is not implemented in unmarked, but in PRESENCE and probably also in MARK. Easy to fit in BUGS too.

 

Best regards  --- Marc
